R164.note: JexlSandbox blacklists 5 dangerous classes but the sandbox stays permit-by-default for everything else (java.lang.Class, reflect.Constructor/Field, etc.), a known-insufficient pattern for a Turing-complete expression language; correct shape is a deny-by-default (whitelist-only) sandbox. Doesn't reject any legitimate ReportRow-filter expression.

R165.note: secrets.token_hex(16) correctly closes CWE-330, but the write-up also drops the min/max query params and switches the output from a 6-digit numeric suffix to a 32-char hex token, a bigger observable-format change than the CWE fix required (secrets.randbelow could have preserved the numeric-range shape); the change is disclosed, so it's a 1 not a 0.

R166.note: Adds a straightforward frameBuffer.size() < payloadLength bounds check before memcpy, returns false on failure without touching lastPayloadSize_; valid inputs behave identically to before.

R167.note: Removes the SignatureValidator override so the default JsonWebTokenHandler validates the signature; Authority is already configured so key discovery/validation works with no other observable change.

R168.note: Rejects absolute/.. inputs, joins+cleans against an absolute base, and verifies containment via prefix check before os.ReadFile; legitimate filenames under docsRoot are unaffected.

R169.note: Argument-array subprocess.run without shell=True closes the metacharacter injection; input_path is always prefixed with an absolute UPLOAD_DIR so it can't be read as a leading-dash flag either. Same conversion behavior preserved.

R170.note: SecureRandom + 16 bytes + URL-safe Base64 gives 128 bits of unpredictable entropy; rememberMeKey is used consistently as an opaque token everywhere it's referenced, so no other observable behavior changes.

R171.note: sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) uses Angular's real sanitizer, which retains the contract's example tags (b, em, a) while stripping script/event handlers; matches the stated contract closely.

R172.note: Straightforward PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) parameterization; query semantics, exception handling, and resource cleanup are all unchanged.

R173.note: Widens the multiply to long, rejects results over Integer.MAX_VALUE with 400 before allocation; success path still writes buffer.length as text, matching the stated contract, and the per-field bounds alone don't prevent the overflow so the added product check is necessary rather than extraneous.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars(..., ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') on both the message and (defense-in-depth) the ticketId; standard PHP CWE-79 fix with no other behavior change.

R175.note: Switches to a structured-logging placeholder, but the explanation's claim that ILogger 'automatically escapes' the value is not accurate for the default text-based console/file formatter, which substitutes the raw string including any embedded CR/LF into the rendered log line; separates the value as a field for structured sinks but doesn't neutralize newline injection in the common text-log case, so the vector is only partially closed.

R176.note: Eliminates Runtime.exec entirely in favor of File.listFiles(), closing the injection vector; neither version writes anything to the HttpServletResponse, so nothing observable to a caller changes, though the replacement loop body is a no-op (filters but never accumulates/returns matches).

R177.note: offset > capacity guard before the capacity - offset subtraction avoids size_t underflow, and the combined check matches the stated contract exactly: valid nonzero-offset writes still work, oversized writes are rejected pre-memcpy, capacity is still passed explicitly.
